summary: The crew breaks up from watching the screens. Mouse asks what it means; Switch says it means nothing, and Cypher remarks that everyone falls the first time, addressing Trinity, but she she has already departed. Neo's eyes flutter open as Tank removes the plug.; Neo tries to move, groans, and cradles Neo cradles his ribs. As Tank assists Morpheus, Neo spits blood into his palm. says he thought it wasn't real; Morpheus answers that his Neo gazes at the blood. and asks whether dying in the Matrix means dying here. Morpheus replies that the body cannot live without the mind.

what_changes.before: believes the Matrix is not real and that harm there is not real
what_changes.after: learns his mind makes it real and that death there kills the body
what_changes.evidence: NEO: I thought it wasn't real. MORPHEUS

what_changes.before: still plugged in and upright after the failed jump
what_changes.after: unplugged, injured, groaning and cradling his ribs
what_changes.evidence: Neo's eyes open as Tank eases the

event_hint.one_line: Neo is pulled from the failed jump program and learns the real danger of dying in the Matrix.

objects_that_matter: the blood Neo spits into his hand

minds.wants: To understand what just happened to him — to have the failure explained in terms that let him believe the rules are survivable.
minds.feels: A physical shock (injured ribs, blood in his own mouth) colliding with a conceptual shock. The training was abstract until his body answered it with real pain; now he is running the one question that matters to him — whether this can kill him — while trying to keep his composure in front of the crew.
minds.shows: Groaning, cradling his ribs, spitting blood into his hand, then asking two calm, direct questions. He lets them see the injury but keeps the fear in the phrasing — he frames it as a hypothetical ('if you are killed'), not 'can I die.'
minds.basis: He tries to move and immediately groans and cradles his ribs; he spits blood into his hand before speaking. His line 'I thought it wasn't real' answers directly to sc-059/061 where the jump was a mental exercise, and his second question follows his eyes fixing on the blood — the visible proof that it IS real. The shift from 'it' to 'you'/'here' shows him personalizing the danger while keeping it at one remove.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a reliable guide who will tell him the truth about the danger before putting him in more of it.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus's answers are true but minimal and delivered without reassurance; he withholds the comfort Neo is fishing for. Neo does not yet know Morpheus's faith runs ahead of the evidence (cf. ev-016/ev-021, the Oracle), so he is trusting a man whose certainty is partly a wager.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus sees him as a man who just failed a jump.
believes_about.wrong_because: The crew (and Morpheus above all) are invested in Neo as a candidate for something more; the failure is being measured against a hope Neo does not know exists.

minds.wants: To convert Neo's failure into the lesson that matters — that the mind is the real battlefield and death there is death — and to do it without softening it.
minds.feels: Unshaken and deliberate. The failed jump is not a setback to him but the expected next step; his calm is the point he is teaching. Under it, a steadiness that comes from faith, not from this particular outcome.
minds.shows: Two short, oracular statements ('Your mind makes it real'; 'The body cannot live without the mind'). He does not fuss over Neo's injury or offer comfort; he lets Tank do the physical tending while he does the teaching.
minds.basis: He answers Neo's emotional 'I thought it wasn't real' with a principle, not reassurance. While Tank helps him up he is already delivering doctrine. His economy of words matches his rooftop instruction ('Free your mind') — he teaches by statement, not consolation.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is ready to hear the lethal stakes plainly and take them in without breaking.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is still trying to frame death as a hypothetical to keep it at arm's length; he is absorbing the truth in shock, not with the readiness Morpheus's tone assumes.

believes_about.belief: That this failure is ordinary and instructive — 'everyone falls the first time,' the expected curriculum.
believes_about.wrong_because: For Neo specifically Morpheus carries a larger expectation (the One), so the failure is freighted in a way Morpheus will not name aloud here.

minds.wants: To offload his own cynicism and get a reaction — to have someone confirm that this hope (Neo, the One) is a joke — while pretending he's only making small talk.
minds.feels: Resentment and fatigue with the whole enterprise, already primed (cf. ev-015, where he needles Trinity about Morpheus's faith). The failed jump is, to him, one more proof that the prophecy is a con, and he wants to say it to the one person who'll flinch.
minds.shows: A needling, almost jovial remark — 'Everyone falls the first time, right, Trinity?' — delivered to Trinity's back as she leaves, so it lands as a shrug rather than an argument. He gets no audience and lets the line die.
minds.basis: He addresses Trinity directly, but she has already left — the remark is aimed where it can't be answered, which is exactly the shape of a man who wants to sneer but won't commit to a real fight. His tone matches his skepticism of Morpheus's faith established in ev-015.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is just another kid who's going to get himself killed for Morpheus's delusion — no different from the five before him.
believes_about.wrong_because: He has already decided the answer; he is not observing Neo, he is using Neo as evidence for a conclusion he reached long ago (and will act on in ev-018).

minds.wants: To shut the speculation down — to deny the failure any meaning so it can't become a story the crew gets worked up about.
minds.feels: A flat, practiced cynicism that is really a way of managing disappointment and keeping the operation steady; she won't invest hope in a jump that was never going to work.
minds.shows: One dismissive line — 'It doesn't mean anything' — and then silence. She gives Mouse nothing to build on and offers no reading of her own.
minds.basis: Mouse asks 'What does it mean?' and she answers by refusing the premise entirely. Her terseness matches the crew's earlier transfixed betting (sc-060) — she was watching too, and her 'nothing' is the disciplined end of that excitement.

believes_about.belief: That Neo's failure proves nothing about him one way or the other — he's not special, he's just new.
believes_about.wrong_because: She is right that the jump itself means nothing, but wrong that Neo means nothing; the crew's hidden investment (Morpheus's faith) runs under her dismissal.

minds.wants: A story — he wants the failure to signify something, because he's the one who kept betting 'what if he does.'
minds.feels: Deflated curiosity. He was the engine of hope in sc-060 ('What if he makes it?'), and now he's left holding a question with no satisfying answer, refused by both Switch and Cypher.
minds.shows: A single question ('What does it mean?') and then nothing — he's shut out twice over and drops it.
minds.basis: His question directly continues his role in sc-060, where he pushed the 'what if he makes it' line against Apoc's certainty. Here he gets 'nothing' from Switch and an unanswered jab from Cypher, so his arc in this beat is the deflation of that hope.

believes_about.belief: That Switch is giving him the real answer — that the failure is meaningless.
believes_about.wrong_because: Switch is managing the crew, not reporting fact; the failure means more than she'll admit, which Mouse can't yet see.

minds.wants: To get both men safely unplugged and on their feet — the practical aftermath, nothing metaphysical.
minds.feels: Focused, competent concern; he's the operator who handles the bodies, so his attention is on the physical recovery, not the lesson.
minds.shows: Easing the plug out of Neo, then moving to help Morpheus up. He says nothing; his care is entirely in the doing.
minds.basis: He performs the two physical actions — removing Neo's plug and helping Morpheus — while everyone else talks. His role throughout has been operational (sc-060 he narrates the odds), so his silence and action here are consistent with being the hands of the crew.

believes_about.belief: That Neo took a hard fall and needs looking after, like any trainee.
believes_about.wrong_because: He shares the crew's quiet stake in Neo as a candidate, so his caretaking is heavier than 'just a trainee' — but he keeps that to himself and works.

connects_back: Neo's 'I thought it wasn't real' resolves the jump program of sc-059/sc-061, where harm was theoretical and the fall was caught by a safety net.
Mouse's 'What does it mean?' and Switch's shutdown continue the transfixed betting of sc-060 (Mouse's 'what if he makes it,' Apoc's 'not possible,' Tank's 'no one's ever made their first jump').
Cypher's needling of Trinity over Morpheus's faith in ev-015 primes his 'everyone falls the first time' jab here — same resentment, redirected at the failed jump.
Tank easing the plug and helping Morpheus is the operational follow-through to the crew watching the screens in sc-060.
sets_up: ev-016 (Street Training and the Agent Ambush): Neo now knows death in the Matrix is real death, which is the stakes under every later simulation where Agents can kill him.

ev-018 (Cypher's Warning and Betrayal): Cypher's established cynicism about Morpheus's candidates, voiced here in miniature, matures into telling Neo that five previous 'Ones' died — the same 'everyone falls' worldview turned into a warning and then betrayal.
ev-021 (The Oracle's Prophecy): Morpheus's willingness to state lethal stakes plainly, without reassurance, is of a piece with the faith that will carry Neo to the Oracle despite the body count.
Neo's shift from treating the Matrix as unreal to treating his mind as the real battlefield sets the conceptual foundation for every subsequent lesson about bending and surviving the rules.
dramatic_function: To convert a physical training failure into the story's central rule — that the mind makes the Matrix real and death there is death — while letting the crew's differing attitudes toward Neo (hope, cynicism, dismissal, care) register in the aftermath, and to harden the stakes just as Neo begins to matter to everyone.
